stories.headline: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 4
stories.summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up through three weeks of the season? Plus, we picked out each team's biggest fantasy surprise -- good or bad.
stories.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season was filled with close matchups. There were 12 such games on Sunday, tying the most matchups decided by eight or fewer points in a single day in NFL history, per ESPN Research.

Along with those close contests came plenty of intriguing fantasy performances. So in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to look at every team's fantasy football surprise (good or bad) this season. They went off ESPN Fantasy's draft rankings, average draft position (ADP) and current scoring leaders in PPR leagues.

To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

The 3-0 Raiders are shooting up our list, climbing up six spots after doing the same last week. They're the first team in the common draft era (since 1967) to start 3-0 after drafting a QB No. 1 (Fernando Mendoza) in the previous draft, per ESPN Research. And against the Saints, they broke a franchise-worst 39-game streak of regular-season games without scoring 30 points.
New England fell six more spots after quarterback Drake Maye registered a 15.5 Total QBR in a blowout loss to the Jaguars -- a career worst with at least 15 dropbacks. Through three games, the Patriots' offense is averaging the lowest EPA per play and points per drive by any team since the 2023 Jets, who had Zach Wilson at QB, per ESPN Research.
After starting 0-3, the Buccaneers are ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. This is the team's worst record to begin a season since 2014, when it finished 2-14 in its first year under current general manager Jason Licht. And things might not get easier for the Bucs, who are expected to play undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) for at least the next three weeks.

Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

1. Buffalo Bills (3-0)
Week 3 result: Beat the Chargers 24-16

Week 3 ranking: 1

Fantasy surprise: TE Dalton Kincaid

Through three weeks, Kincaid leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and has caught 14 of the 17 passes thrown his way. He ranks top 10 among tight ends in targets, posting the best catch percentage (82.4%) of any tight end or wide receiver with at least that many targets. Not bad for someone who was ranked as TE15 in ESPN's preseason rankings. -- Nick Suss

2. San Francisco 49ers (3-0)
Week 3 result: Beat the Cardinals 36-30

Week 3 ranking: 3

Fantasy surprise: TE George Kittle

Under normal circumstances, it would not be a surprise to see Kittle as the TE4 in fantasy. But given that he tore his right Achilles on Jan. 11 and missed all of training camp, that he returned in Week 1 close to his usual self is a testament to his passion for the game. And the Niners have needed every bit of his production to help weather the storm of injuries elsewhere. Kittle ranks fifth among all tight ends in receiving yards (174), 11th in receptions (12) and tied for first in touchdowns (three). -- Nick Wagoner

3. Kansas City Chiefs (3-0)
Week 3 result: Beat the Dolphins 24-10

Week 3 ranking: 4

Fantasy surprise: RB Kenneth Walker III

Most fantasy owners knew Walker was a good choice, especially after his impressive postseason run to help the Seahawks win the Super Bowl. But not even the Chiefs could have expected this level of production from Walker, who has the second-most total fantasy points at RB this season. He has already produced 442 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns. Walker is the first player in franchise history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within the first three weeks, per ESPN Research. -- Nate Taylor

4. Seattle Seahawks (2-1)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Commanders 33-31

Week 3 ranking: 2

Fantasy surprise: RB Jadarian Price

Price was 25th among running backs in ADP, reflecting the fact that he was going to be part of a timeshare in Seattle's backfield. But even with those modest expectations, the rookie first-round pick is off to an underwhelming start. He ranks 47th in fantasy points among running backs after a dud of a performance in Week 3, when he totaled 22 scrimmage yards on six touches and a lost fumble. The lost fumble was Price's second in as many weeks, which was a big reason for his diminished workload. -- Brady Henderson

5. Baltimore Ravens (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Cowboys 34-31

Week 3 ranking: 7

Fantasy surprise: TE Mark Andrews

Andrews had surrendered the title of Lamar Jackson's No. 1 target to WR Zay Flowers, but there was hope that Andrews would remain an option in the red zone. He has only one red zone target on eight routes run this season. Now, he is dealing with a hand injury that limited his playing time in Week 3. Andrews, who was ranked as the TE14 before the season, is currently 19th in scoring at his position. -- Jamison Hensley

6. Denver Broncos (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Rams 30-26

Week 3 ranking: 8

Fantasy surprise: WR Courtland Sutton

The Broncos' offensive struggles, especially in first halves, have dragged down everybody's numbers. They haven't found a rhythm much of the time, and save for Jaylen Waddle's 138-yard effort against the Jaguars in Week 2, the WRs have been caught up in the wash (Pat Bryant has the group's only TD catch). Sutton, who is second in targets to Waddle with 16, could be seen as the biggest disappointment. He has yet to eclipse more than 10 fantasy points in any game. -- Jeff Legwold

7. Los Angeles Rams (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Broncos 30-26

Week 3 ranking: 5

Fantasy surprise: WR Puka Nacua

Despite missing part of training camp with a psoas injury, Nacua had an ADP of 9.0. But he has played only in Week 1 because of a groin injury, putting up 12.4 points in PPR leagues. On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the injury "has impacted [Nacua's] explosiveness." Last week, coach Sean McVay said that barring a setback, the expectation is that Nacua will be able to play in Week 4 against the Eagles. -- Sarah Barshop

8. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Bears 27-7

Week 3 ranking: 6

Fantasy surprise: WR Dontayvion Wicks

Wicks has the second-most receptions (nine) and receiving yards (179) on the team behind DeVonta Smith. He is currently the WR30 in fantasy. There was some thought heading into the summer that rookie Makai Lemon could ascend to the No. 2 role, but injuries left him on the sideline for most of camp. In the meantime, Wicks and QB Jalen Hurts developed a comfort level with one another, which has been on display early this season, including in high-leverage moments. -- Tim McManus

9. Minnesota Vikings (3-0)
Week 3 result: Beat the Buccaneers 23-16

Week 3 ranking: 12

Fantasy surprise: WR Justin Jefferson

Jefferson had an ADP of 13.4, but he has had only one fantasy-productive game for a variety of reasons. That came in Week 1, when he caught two touchdown passes from backup quarterback Carson Wentz (31.2 fantasy points). The Vikings played their Week 2 game at rainy Soldier Field, and in Week 3, Jefferson played only one series before departing with an ankle injury. Jefferson could be back as soon as next Sunday against the Dolphins, but with the Vikings' offense struggling as much as any in the NFL, it's unclear if Jefferson can get back on track. -- Kevin Seifert

10. Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Patriots 35-6

Week 3 ranking: 13

Fantasy surprise: WR Brian Thomas Jr.

With Parker Washington's emergence and the reliability of Jakobi Meyers, the targets were expected to be spread out somewhat evenly among Jacksonville's receivers. But Thomas had a great offseason and the Jaguars wanted to push the ball downfield more, so expectations were high for the WR40 in our preseason projections. Now, Thomas has just seven catches for 88 yards and no TDs. Rookie Josh Cameron (two TD catches) has earned almost equal playing time, too. At this point, it's almost impossible to expect consistent fantasy production out of Thomas. -- Michael DiRocco

11. Chicago Bears (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Eagles 27-7

Week 3 ranking: 11

Fantasy surprise: WR Kalif Raymond

At best, the 11-year NFL veteran was considered a waiver wire add in the preseason given his status at WR108. With a group of Chicago playmakers highlighted by Colston Loveland, Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze, Raymond wasn't projected to factor into a significant portion of the Bears' target share, but that went out the window quickly. Through three games, Raymond leads the Bears with 21 targets, which he turned into 19 catches for 214 yards and a touchdown. He has twice been his team's leading receiver (wins over Carolina and Philadelphia). Raymond ranks 12th among wide receivers in fantasy production (15.5 fantasy points per game), and his production on punt returns adds to his overall fantasy value. -- Courtney Cronin

12. Cincinnati Bengals (2-1)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Steelers 30-27

Week 3 ranking: 9

Fantasy surprise: RB Chase Brown

Brown was the RB8 in ESPN's preseason rankings and someone who was going to be a major part of Cincinnati's offense. The latter part of that has materialized, as he is second on the team with 229 scrimmage yards (197 rushing, 32 receiving) and has 13 targets (seventh most among RBs). But that hasn't led to big points for fantasy managers. Brown has just one offensive touchdown, with a season high of 18.8 fantasy points in Week 1 against the Bucs. -- Ben Baby

13. Detroit Lions (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Jets 31-24

Week 3 ranking: 14

Fantasy surprise: QB Jared Goff

It's sometimes easy to forget about Goff's consistency because he plays alongside elite playmakers such as RB Jahmyr Gibbs and WR Amon-Ra St. Brown. The veteran QB is a viable starter in fantasy this season, averaging 21.9 points. Goff was the 18th-best quarterback in our draft rankings and had an ADP of 131.4. After Sunday's win, Gibbs lauded Goff as Detroit's "leader." "We trust him with everything," Gibbs said. -- Eric Woodyard

14. Las Vegas Raiders (3-0)
Week 3 result: Beat the Saints 35-27

Week 3 ranking: 20

Fantasy surprise: RB Ashton Jeanty

Jeanty got off to a strong start, recording 32.7 fantasy points in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins. But he has been inconsistent since then, averaging fewer than 3.0 yards per carry and 11.3 fantasy points in the past two games. Jeanty was expected to make a significant jump in Year 2 under new coach Klint Kubiak. His production should pick up if he gets more opportunities in the passing game, though Brock Bowers just returned for the Raiders from a meniscus trim. -- Ryan McFadden

15. Dallas Cowboys (2-1)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Ravens 34-31

Week 3 ranking: 16

Fantasy surprise: WR George Pickens

Pickens looked great in training camp, and he was the WR12 in our draft rankings. So it's surprising to see he has not scored or registered a catch for at least 20 yards. His production was better against Baltimore (seven catches, 82 yards), but the Cowboys need to get Pickens involved more. A team that lived on big plays in 2025 hasn't been as effective on them this year. Pickens is averaging just 9.6 yards per catch, and he has gone five straight games without a touchdown. -- Todd Archer

16. New England Patriots (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Jaguars 35-6

Week 3 ranking: 10

Fantasy surprise: QB Drake Maye

Maye had an ADP of 61.2, which ranked him as the fifth-highest QB. But he has just one TD pass while throwing six interceptions, bringing him to 15 turnovers in seven games since the start of last season's playoffs. Maye has yet to put up double-digit fantasy points in a game this season. He badly misses WR1 A.J. Brown (on IR with a high ankle sprain), and when the running game can't gain traction like this past Sunday, things get shaky quickly. -- Mike Reiss

17. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Bengals 30-27

Week 3 ranking: 25

Fantasy surprise: WR DK Metcalf

None of Pittsburgh's skill position players was projected to be a significant fantasy contributor, but Metcalf (WR31 in ADP) largely underperformed through the first three weeks with multiple drops, 11 catches and 98 receiving yards. Metcalf, though, might be turning a corner with the rest of the Steelers' offense after finally recording a touchdown catch against the Bengals. He put up 12.1 fantasy points in the win. -- Brooke Pryor

18. New Orleans Saints (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Raiders 35-27

Week 3 ranking: 19

Fantasy surprise: QB Tyler Shough

Shough was ranked No. 17 in our draft rankings, but his 69.38 fantasy points are third among quarterbacks behind Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. Shough is currently second in passing yards (917), tied for third in passing TDs (eight), first in attempts (132), and first in completions (91). While there have been negatives (three turnovers versus the Raiders and tied for second in sacks), Shough has consistently put up big fantasy numbers every week. -- Katherine Terrell

19. New York Giants (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Titans 12-7

Week 3 ranking: 18

Fantasy surprise: WR Malik Nabers

Nabers has had a slow start to the season coming off a serious knee injury, recording 12 catches for 96 yards. The explosiveness isn't all the way back yet, with his longest reception being 16 yards. Nabers called himself "rusty" after Week 1. He still appears to be knocking it off, as evidenced by currently being the WR56 in fantasy. Nabers also has to get right and build chemistry with new starting quarterback Jameis Winston. They didn't spend much time this summer working together. -- Jordan Raanan

20. Green Bay Packers (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Falcons 35-14

Week 3 ranking: 17

Fantasy surprise: TE Tucker Kraft

Coming off last season's torn ACL, Kraft was ranked ninth among tight ends in our draft rankings. Through three games, he's 27th in fantasy points at the position. Kraft has just nine catches for 108 yards and no touchdowns despite not being on a snap limit. As bad as the Packers' offensive line has been, the Packers still rank tied for fourth in the NFL in passing yards per game. But Kraft has not been a big part of that. -- Rob Demovsky

21. Houston Texans (0-3)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Colts 19-17

Week 3 ranking: 15

Fantasy surprise: RB David Montgomery

After 28.9 fantasy points in Week 1, Montgomery has only 11.2 in the past two games combined. He averages 0.5 yards before contact -- an abhorrent number for a rushing attack. Any hope for an improvement in Montgomery's fantasy production starts with better play from the offensive line. That unit is a big reason the Texans are winless and averaging 11.5 points per game over the past two weeks. -- DJ Bien-Aime

22. Carolina Panthers (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Browns 21-18

Week 3 ranking: 21

Fantasy surprise: QB Bryce Young

Despite a somewhat underwhelming Week 3 performance, Young is averaging 313 passing yards and 2.3 passing touchdowns per game in 2026. That has made him the QB4 in fantasy, behind Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Tyler Shough. An impressive start considering Young was the QB18 in ADP. Young is up 1.5 yards per passing attempt from 2025 to 2026. While he is not rushing as much as he has in the past, he has one rushing TD on three carries this season. -- Mike Kaye

23. Indianapolis Colts (1-2)
Week 3 result: Beat the Texans 19-17

Week 3 ranking: 24

Fantasy surprise: QB Daniel Jones

Jones has held his own after tearing an Achilles less than 10 months ago, but a couple of realities have made him a less-than-ideal fantasy quarterback compared with 2025. First, Jones has had an interception in each game. Additionally, he has thrown three touchdown passes for a 3.1% TD rate -- down from 4.9% in 2025. Finally, Jones' five rushing touchdowns last season were a nice bonus, but he has not rushed into the end zone in 2026. He is currently ranked 29th among QBs in fantasy, with a season high of 11.4 points in Week 2. -- Stephen Holder

24. Cleveland Browns (2-1)
Week 3 result: Beat the Panthers 21-18

Week 3 ranking: 29

Fantasy surprise: QB Deshaun Watson

Expectations were low for Watson, who had performed like one of the worst NFL quarterbacks since joining Cleveland in 2022 and was returning from two Achilles tears. His ADP had him ranked as the QB29, but he's the QB10 so far this season. Watson's passing numbers (587 yards, five touchdowns) are modest, but he has turned the ball over only once, and he's using his legs well. His 105 rushing yards are the fourth most among quarterbacks. -- Daniel Oyefusi

25. New York Jets (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Lions 31-24

Week 3 ranking: 27

Fantasy surprise: TE Kenyon Sadiq

Who needs training camp? The rookie figured to get off to a slow start after missing nearly all of camp due to a hernia injury, but he already has 12 catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns (one receiving, one rushing). He's 10th among tight ends in fantasy points, and his role should continue to grow as he gains a better grasp of the offense. Sadiq has already developed good chemistry with QB Geno Smith. -- Rich Cimini

26. Washington Commanders (1-2)
Week 3 result: Beat the Seahawks 33-31

Week 3 ranking: 28

Fantasy surprise: WR Stefon Diggs

Diggs was the WR33 in ADP, but he's up to WR13 as Washington's leader in receptions (13) and receiving touchdowns (three). He didn't sign with the Commanders until after the first week of training camp, and he's now already with his second quarterback. The question is: Where does he go from here? He has been more of an underneath receiver, as he is yet to surpass 55 yards in a single game. Diggs posted five 100-yard games with New England last season. -- John Keim

27. Los Angeles Chargers (0-3)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Bills 24-16

Week 3 ranking: 22

Fantasy surprise: RB Omarion Hampton

Expectations were high for the 2025 first-round pick, given how running backs have thrived with OC Mike McDaniel at other stops. But Hampton has been a disappointment so far. He was the 12th running back in ADP, but his 31 points rank 22nd. Hampton also saw a decreased workload in Week 3 after struggles in his first two weeks. As the Chargers move forward, this could become more of a split backfield with Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, who averaged 6.5 yards per carry to Hampton's 3.7 in Buffalo. -- Kris Rhim

28. Arizona Cardinals (1-2)
Week 3 result: Lost to the 49ers 36-30

Week 3 ranking: 26

Fantasy surprise: QB Jacoby Brissett

Brissett is on 4.5% of ESPN rosters and is the QB16 after Sunday's loss. That might be middle of the pack of the 32 starters, but it's surprising when considering he was ranked 50th among quarterbacks in ADP. Brissett is averaging 16.2 points per game, which is 39th overall in the entire league. He was ranked 361st overall before the season started. -- Josh Weinfuss

29. Atlanta Falcons (1-2)
Week 3 result: Beat the Packers 35-14

Week 3 ranking: 31

Fantasy surprise: TE Kyle Pitts Sr.

Pitts was one of the most productive tight ends last season and a boon for fantasy players. He was the 10th tight end taken in ESPN drafts, but he has 1.3 fantasy points so far. Part of it has not been his fault. The Falcons' offense was a mess the first two weeks with third-string quarterback Cooper Rush. There is hope for Pitts with the return of Michael Penix Jr. Yet, he had only one catch for 5 yards in Penix's Week 3 debut. -- Marc Raimondi

30. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Vikings 23-16

Week 3 ranking: 23

Fantasy surprise: WR Ted Hurst III

Hurst is currently the WR56 in fantasy and has the second-most targets among the Bucs' wide receivers -- behind Emeka Egbuka and ahead of Chris Godwin Jr. The rookie third-round pick has six catches on 13 targets with a touchdown, while Godwin has 10 catches on 12 targets and saw a would-be touchdown against the Vikings wiped off the board due to a holding call. With Jalen McMillan sidelined for several weeks, Hurst will continue to hear his number called. But consistency has been an issue, as he has caught only 46.2% of his targets. -- Jenna Laine

31. Tennessee Titans (0-3)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Giants 12-7

Week 3 ranking: 30

Fantasy surprise: WR Wan'Dale Robinson

There really wasn't much expected fantasywise for any Titans players, but Robinson drew interest (rostered in 64.4% of ESPN leagues) primarily because he had 90-plus receptions in each of the past two seasons in New York under Brian Daboll (the current Titans OC). But through three games, Robinson has 13 receptions on 18 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. He was targeted 11 times against the Giants, so maybe a turnaround is on the way. -- Turron Davenport

32. Miami Dolphins (0-3)
Week 3 result: Lost to the Chiefs 24-10

Week 3 ranking: 32

Fantasy surprise: WR Malik Washington

There aren't many (any?) Dolphins players who were drafted with an expectation to produce in fantasy outside of the injured De'Von Achane (torn ACL). But Washington has quietly been consistent this season. He was drafted as WR71 but is 30 spots higher entering Week 4. Washington averages just north of seven targets per game; he has at least four catches or 50 receiving yards in each game he has played. With Achane out for the season, the Dolphins might become more of a short, quick passing offense -- and Washington figures to be a beneficiary of that. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

stories.headline: Ferrari gives Fred Vasseur 'full confidence' amid Christian Horner speculation
stories.summary: Ferrari has insisted it has "full confidence" in Fred Vasseur amid mounting speculation about both his job and the potential of Christian Horner replacing him.
stories.body:
Ferrari has insisted it has "full confidence" in Fred Vasseur amid mounting speculation about both his job and the potential of Christian Horner replacing him.

In a hastily-arranged virtual news conference on Tuesday, Ferrari's chief communication officer Maria Conti said the team -- under-pressure due to poor results on the track -- wanted to avoid any "gossip" moving forwards.

"We have confidence -- full confidence -- in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so," she said. "At this time it's really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.

"Ferrari has always attracted extraordinary interest, and it's only natural that many professionals aspire to be part of it. It is a reflection of the strength of what Ferrari really represents.

"So, this is why we really want to avoid, and we do not intend to fuel speculation or comment on assumptions coming from outside the company.

"And it's not just related to the story in the times of Mr. Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred."

An interview Horner had given The Times, published ahead of last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, took on a life of its own ahead of the Baku event. Horner's interview, which had been primarily to promote his new autobiography, out next month, included a response to a question about whether he would take the Ferrari job.

Horner replied: "Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It's the dream. And arguably it's the sleeping giant of Formula 1." ESPN understands the former Red Bull boss was not intending to use the Times interview to declare his interest in Vasseur's job and has been told by sources he is not actively pursuing a job with the Italian job as things stand, nor has he been offered one. Either way, the quote dominated the build-up and aftermath of the Baku race.

After Saturday's event, a frustrated Vasseur said he had been asked "25 times a day" about his job and the Horner link.

The speculation around Vasseur and Ferrari leadership has reached fever pitch recently as the team's performances have slumped.

Earlier this month, Lewis Hamilton posted to Instagram to deny multiple reports in Italy that he was pushing for changes to be made to senior members of the race team -- the seven-time world champion said he still backed Vasseur after the Baku race.

Tuesday's press conference comes ahead of a race in Malaysia -- F1 is in the middle of the first of three triple headers (nine races across 11 weekends) to close out the season Conti added that while news about Ferrari is not uncommon, it was time to draw a line in the sand underneath it so the team can focus on the remainder of the season.

- Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto after calling for ban

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

"We are doing that today, on Tuesday 29th of September, because we would like to avoid that the next weekend in Malaysia will be focused only on this kind of gossip and speculation. But we would like to be focused on the race, on the performance, on the team, on Fred," Conti added.

"The storm of communication around the team -- we are used to that, Ferrari is used to that.

"With more than 21 social media channels covering all the company, the fact is that after the race and on Sunday and yesterday, we can say this storm of communication was increasing. Normally it's going down.

"And as we have a race the next weekend in Malaysia, we would like to take the time to ask you kindly not to focus on this. Fred is in his position and we are confirming his leadership. And we would like to be focused on the race, the team and its leadership.

"This is why we have done it. Because looking and monitoring the communication yesterday, today, normally it's going down. But everybody, not just you guys, but also Italian media from all over the world, they are still creating a lot of different stories around Fred.

"And this is not useful. So this is why we decided to do that."

Vassuer has been Ferrari boss since 2023 and almost led the team to a constructors' championship the following season, narrowly missing out to McLaren. He played an instrumental role in signing Hamilton to the team at the start of 2025.

Ferrari started this season looking like the closest challengers to the dominant Mercedes team. Lewis Hamilton won in Spain before Charles Leclerc won in Great Britain, but the team's results have dried up recently. Ferrari has not been on the podium at any of the last five races.

stories.headline: Wayne Rooney wouldn't 'feel comfortable' accepting Premier League medal if Man City stripped of titles
stories.summary: Wayne Rooney has said he wouldn't feel comfortable being handed another Premier League medal if Manchester City are stripped of their title win in the 2011-12 season.
stories.body:
Wayne Rooney has said he wouldn't "feel comfortable" being handed another Premier League medal if Manchester City are stripped of their title win in the 2011-12 season.

City are expected to be found guilty of breaching over 100 of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

Their sanctions are yet to be announced for the alleged financial misconduct but the possibility of the club being stripped of the titles they won during this nine-year period.

They won three Premier League titles in this time, the first of which saw them pip Manchester United on goal difference in the 2011-12 season.

Rio Ferdinand, who was a member of this United team that finished second, has laid claim to Premier League medal but Rooney hasn't followed suit.

"I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal ... I wouldn't really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I'm being honest," he said on his podcast Stick To United.

"I don't think we deserve it, we didn't do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away. The amount of time which has been between it, to accept a Premier League medal ....

"I've seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player's shoes. They are there, doing everything to win a Premier League title and in their minds, they have done it, they have won the Premier League title.

"if that happened to me, if all of a sudden Manchester United had been doing the same and my Premier League medaI had been taken away from, I would be absolutely devastated.

- Joe Hart: I believe Man City chairman claims that club are innocent

- 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports

"It might happen, they might take them away, but I wouldn't want it because I don't think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn't finish first. So when I see ex-teammates and other people saying 'I want a medal' ... I'm happy with the five I've won. I wouldn't want this one, just 15 years later you get a medal because City cheated.

"Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn't feel comfortable accepting it."

stories.headline: Maple Leafs host the Canadiens for first game of 2026 season
stories.summary: Montreal Canadiens vs. Toronto Maple Leafs

Toronto; Tuesday, 7 p.m. EDT


LINE: Canadiens -110, Maple Leafs -111; over/under is 6.5


BOTTOM LINE: The Toronto Maple Leafs host the Montreal Canadiens in the season opener.

stories.headline: Padres and Cubs meet to start the NL Wild Card Series
stories.summary: Chicago Cubs (89-73, second in the NL Central during the regular season) vs. San Diego Padres (91-71, second in the NL West during the regular season)
stories.body:
Chicago Cubs (89-73, second in the NL Central during the regular season) vs. San Diego Padres (91-71, second in the NL West during the regular season)

San Diego; Tuesday, 10 p.m. EDT

PITCHING PROBABLES: Cubs: Matthew Boyd (10-5, 3.91 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, 96 strikeouts); Padres: Michael King (12-10, 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP, 159 strikeouts)

LINE: Padres -128, Cubs +106; over/under is 7 runs

BOTTOM LINE: The San Diego Padres and the Chicago Cubs square off in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series.

stories.headline: Soccer's best 2025-26 kits: The most stylish jerseys you probably missed
stories.summary: While the world's top clubs release their new kits on a wave of hype, there are many more who release absolutely banging jerseys that deserve to be seen.
stories.body:
While the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and all of the Premier League big hitters have their new kits released on a wave of hype, they make up just a small percentage of the soccer jerseys on sale each season.

For every European heavyweight's flashy, expensive launch campaign, there are hundreds of smaller clubs world who have put just as much effort and ingenuity into their new kit concepts and designs for a much smaller audience.

So after casting a discerning eye over the various home, away and third shirts released for the 2026-27 season, we feel it our sworn duty to help showcase some of the finest, most brilliant and super-stylish concepts that have been rolled out by clubs at all levels of the game over the past couple of months.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- A kit fit for the GOAT: Messi's special kit for Argentina farewell

- Premier League 2026-27 kits: Ranking every jersey released

Here, in alphabetical order, is our considered pick of some of the best football kits that you might not have had the pleasure of seeing until now.

Ajax away (Adidas)

Dutch giants Ajax have added yet another beauty to their ever-increasing catalogue of handsome alternative kits. Predominantly black and burnished gold, this shirt also features an elaborate light grey graphic incorporating outlined images of nine of the club's most significant historic achievements; from their four European Cup/UEFA Champions League titles to winning their 30th Eredivisie shield in 2011.

Angers away (Nike)

Exquisite silver-on-silver design from the Ligue 1 side who have used a cool, retro Total 90 template to create a rather special away kit akin to a suit of gleaming futuristic titanium armor.

Atalanta away (New Balance)

This season sees the return of a classic for Atalanta, who have successfully resurrected their glorious white away kit of the late 1980s and early '90s. The modern incarnation retains the zigzag graphic of the original, but reapplies it across the chest with a touch of added contemporary panache.

Celta Vigo third (Hummel)

Celta have traipsed back through their archives in search of inspiration and settled on a gorgeous red diamond pattern inspired by their cult classic 1995-96 "harlequin print" away kit. While still positively oozing with retro appeal, the modern take is even sweeter.

Como home (Adidas)

Como are very much the new kids on the block in the Serie A style stakes, and this season they will be bringing their elegant aesthetic to the Champions League. In essence, the home jersey is a classic polo-style design in blue which mirrors the color of the water of the famous Lake Como. The lines are incredibly clean and the red, white and gold tricolore trim ices the cake perfectly.

FC Basel third (Macron)

Basel seem to swing wildly between the sublime and the ridiculous when it comes to kit designs, but thankfully the Swiss club's 2026-27 third kit is firmly in the former category. The navy ensemble is an amalgam of several of their historic uniforms with the large fold-over collar, subtle pinstriping and delicate jacquard textures all combining to create a refined aesthetic. However, the real star of the show is that ultra cool "whiteout" FCB crest.

Flamengo third (Adidas)

Harking all the way back to Flamengo's original formation as a Rio de Janeiro rowing club in the late 19th Century, the Brazilian side's new third kit is awash with maritime references, most notably the special "oars and anchor" rowing crest that adorns the chest. That same emblem can also be found repeated in the wave pattern that ripples across the entire shirt.

Genoa away (Kappa)

Another kit drawing inspiration from the 19th century, Genoa's pristine new away kit is a love letter to their beginnings as a football and cricket club in 1893. Italy's oldest existing football team have marked that fact with a light cream jersey that resembles the uniforms initially worn by their players before they first adopted their now-familiar Rossoblù (red and blue) half-and-half shirts in 1901. Those colors are referenced in the club crest, kit sponsor logo and sleeve cuffs in a wonderful bit of detailing.

Grimsby Town away (Lotto)

In what might just be the most brazen "homage" of all time, Grimsby have lifted their new away kit directly from mid-'90s AC Milan, replicating the Rossoneri's all-time classic blue-grey and red geometric design in an almost perfect shot-for-shot recreation. Thankfully, Lotto were also responsible for producing those iconic Milan jerseys back in the day, so the Mariners are unlikely to fall foul of any potential plagiarism issues.

Leicester City away (Adidas)

It might coincide with the former Premier League champions' relegation down to the third tier of English football, but the Foxes will at least look glorious on the road in League One this season. Their away kit is inspired by medieval King Richard III (whose remains were famously found beneath a carpark in the city) and comes with royal burgundy flocking and the same lovely retro fox crest worn by the club during the 1980s.

Lyon third (Adidas)

A strong contender for the grooviest football shirt released this season, Lyon paid tribute to their home city's reputation as the hotbed of the French funk music scene by plying their third shirt with psychedelic waves and trippy trim. There is also a repeating circular graphic embossed within the fabric that resembles vinyl records, just to really cement the funky aesthetic.

Monaco third (Mizuno)

Mizuno have made some delightful kits for Monaco in recent years, and the 2026-27 third shirt is no exception. The base color is white, which is then overlaid with a sumptuous minty green graphic that is intended to reflect the sparkling turquoise waters of the natural pools that speckle the picturesque Monegasque coast. It almost brings vibes of a long, hot summer spent idling on the French Riviera.

Os Belenenses home (Hummel)

One of the oldest sporting clubs in Portugal, Belenenses have gone all the way back to the beginning and drummed up a delightful retro home kit. As well as featuring their classic royal blue club colors and red cross crest, it also carries a mosaic graphic pattern made up of miniature tiles detailing individual elements of their own history and local culture, architecture and identity -- from sailing ships to cathedrals.

Sheffield Wednesday away (Umbro)

It's tough to pick a winner between Sheffield Wednesday's new retro home and away kits, but we think the lean and lovely yellow and black away jersey just about pips it. Umbro have reprised and modernized their designs from the 1992-93 season, which were the last they provided for the Owls before Puma stepped in for the decade that followed.

Strasbourg away (Adidas)

Another strong contender for kit of the year, Strasbourg's away shirt is once again a deliberate recreation of a retro classic. Nostalgia aside, the reworking is a vast improvement on the 1994-96 original, with extra light blue hues helping to create a more delicate diamond pattern which works wonderfully well to frame the oval-shaped heritage RCS crest, which was first worn by the club between 1920 and 1945.

SV Wehen Wiesbaden away (Errea)

German third-tier outfit Wiesbaden are punching well above their weight here. Their away kit is adorned with the famed art nouveau stylings of their home city, which boasts a plethora of ornately decorated buildings, municipal halls, galleries and museums. The result is a lush, verdant green jersey which is festooned with ornate floral motifs and highlighted with lovely bronze flecks here and there.

TSV Eintracht Braunschweig third (Umbro)

Using the slate grey shield of the Braunschweig coat of arms as a jumping-off point, the German second-tier side have concocted a smart kit that looks like it has been plucked straight out of the 1980s. The tonal muted greys are nicely balanced and allow the pops of color on the crest and trim to stand out.

Venezia home (Nocta)

One of an increasing number of clubs who have turned to fashion and streetwear labels to help create their kits, this season's offerings from Venezia are the third produced by Nike's Drake-affiliated brand Nocta. They might also be the best yet, with the diagonally split orange and green bar across the midriff of the home shirt providing a particularly cool "billboard" for the sponsor logo.

VfB Stuttgart away, Europe (Jako)

To coincide with their return to the Champions League, Stuttgart have revived one of the most symbolic kits to feature in their European history. Indeed, the red shirt worn during a UEFA Cup first-round game against Banyasz Tatabanya back in 1988 is an artefact of Europe's history, in a way.

Several hundred intrepid Stuttgart fans made the trip from the former West Germany behind the Iron Curtain to Hungary to watch their side lose 2-1 on the night, only to advance to the second round on aggregate.

The German club decided to reward their raucous travelling support by doling out all of the players' match-worn kit among the away section after the final whistle. Stuttgart then battled to the 1988-89 UEFA Cup final, only to narrowly lose out against Diego Maradona's Napoli over two legs.

After being given away to fans, the "Tatabanya" kit was never worn again -- but almost 40 years later, the same red lozenge pattern has been resurrected to help instill the same resilience on Stuttgart's latest continental quest. A mini-history lesson, and also a work of true retro brilliance.

stories.headline: Five stats: Why USMNT should be excited about Cavan Sullivan
stories.summary: Is the hype around Cavan Sullivan's USMNT future too much? No, it's actually not enough -- and here are five reasons why.
stories.body:
There's something incredible happening in MLS right now, and the average World Cup watcher probably has no clue.

Seriously, think about all of the people you know who are "sports fans" but maybe not "soccer fans" -- the ones who root hard for the U.S. men's national team every four years and know the names of their four or five best players.

Sure, they probably still can't pronounce the last name of manager Mauricio Pochettino, but they watched tons of soccer this summer. The World Cup had so many games, and finally, it was all aligned with our time zones. These people now have opinions about VAR, England's prevent defense and the general moral fiber of the Argentina national team.

They're primed to care about soccer, especially American soccer, and especially a kind of greatness we've never seen before from a player of a certain age. No, I'm not talking about Lionel Messi, who somehow (1) might still be the greatest soccer player in the world, (2) is easily the greatest 39-year-old soccer player we've ever seen, and (3) continues to play soccer every week, across North America, without having any effect on North American sports discourse.

No, I'm talking about Cavan Sullivan, the 16-year-old phenom who, somehow, still feels as if he's being underhyped.

The history of American soccer is filled with players who were overpromised and couldn't do anything but underdeliver, but this is different. It's not just that we, Americans, have never seen someone like Sullivan. No, the wider soccer world -- the rest of the entire world -- rarely ever sees someone like Sullivan.

Here are some numbers for why you should get excited:

1,675 minutes
As I like to often say: The best predictor of future stardom is minutes players at a young age.

Take the three front-runners for this year's Ballon d'Or. Harry Kane was playing and scoring goals for Millwall in the Championship during his age-18 season. Lamine Yamal is 19 -- right now. And Kylian Mbappé broke out for Monaco during his age-17 season.

Sullivan is currently in his age-16 season (defined by your age at the start of the campaign). And so far, he has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

The site FBref has data for what they call the "Next 14" -- essentially, the most competitive leagues in the world after Europe's Big Five -- that goes back to the beginning of the current century, if not more. Only 21 outfield players have played more league minutes than Sullivan, who still has at least eight games left in his season. If we expand the dataset to include the Big Five, then only five other players -- Eduardo Camavinga, Alex Song, Gavi, Lamine Yamal, and Nuri Sahin -- have played more minutes than Sullivan before their age-17 season.

The leader, among all of these players? Freddy Adu had played 5,448 minutes by the end of his age-16 season.

€1.54 billion
Though we don't have much useful leaguewide data dating to 2006, when Adu was wrapping up his age-16 season, I do feel confident in saying the following: MLS is a lot better than it was 20 years ago.

Heck, it's a lot better than it was even 10 years ago. Per a recent analysis by Michael Caley: In 2016, the average combined transfer value of the median MLS team (as estimated by the site Transfermarkt) was significantly lower than the average team in the first divisions in Mexico, Belgium, Portugal and the Netherlands. Since then, the league has essentially caught up to Belgium and Mexico in transfer value, and it has surpassed Portugal and the Netherlands.

Though the biggest teams in those European leagues are still way better and richer than any MLS side -- thanks to Champions League prize money -- the average match that Cavan Sullivan plays in MLS is probably tougher than what he'd face were he playing for Benfica, Porto or PSV.

All in all, the combined estimated transfer values of all 30 MLS clubs is €1.54 billion -- or about €51.3 million per team.

12 goals and assists
For the Big Five leagues, FBref has goal-and-assist data dating to at least the mid-1990s for Ligue 1, for the entirety of the Premier League since its breakaway from the English Football League in 1992, and the late 1980s for Italy, Germany and Spain.

Over that stretch, the record for goals+assists before a player's age-17 season comes from Bojan Krkic, who scored 10 goals and created three more in his early years -- right at the beginning of Pep Guardiola's dominance with Barcelona. Next after him is a tie between Yamal and Wayne Rooney's Everton years, at 10.

Sullivan currently has 12 -- a nearly even split between seven goals and five assists. If we expand the list out to the Next 14 leagues, then only four players have more. Chelsea's Estêvão registered 23 goal contributions with Palmeiras in Brazil's top flight -- a much tougher league than MLS. Normally, I'd remove penalties from the equation, but the fact that Estevao was chosen to take three penalties as a 16-year-old feels like useful information.

Then there's Adu with 22, Romelu Lukaku with 19 for Anderlecht, and Endrick's 15 with Palmeiras before he moved to Real Madrid.

The smart money is on Sullivan moving up the list over the next month as MLS wraps up its regular season. In his eight games since the World Cup, he has scored six goals and added four assists.

132 passes into the attacking third
Sullivan is the rare attacking prospect whose attacking production actually underrates his track record.

Of course, the production at this point in his career is fantastic -- bested only by a collection of some of the best attacking prospects of the past 30 years. But that production is backed up by a sustainable drumbeat of quality shots and chances created, plus a bedrock of excellent ball progression and off-ball movement.

To dig into some more advanced numbers, we need to move beyond FBref's historical database. Stats Perform doesn't have numbers that extend to the 1990s, but we're able to look at the Big Five in Europe, MLS, Liga MX, the Dutch Eredivisie, the English second division, a number of cup competitions in Europe and South America, plus the first divisions in Portugal, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. The data dates to at least the mid-2010s.

Among all of the players who fall within there, Sullivan ranks third and second, respectively, in the two most important and predictive attacking metrics: expected goals and expected assists. The other players I've highlighted in the below chart, which only looks at minutes played at age 16 or earlier, mostly played in more difficult leagues, but across the modern era of the sport almost no one has done what Sullivan is currently doing, still eight years away from the start of his prime:

He's also not just standing up near the goal and waiting for things to happen. Among this same cohort, Sullivan leads all players in passes played into the attacking third, with 132. The only other players with more than 100 are Jude Bellingham (104) and Gilberto Mora (109), both of whom are midfielders, not attackers.

That's clear when we look at passes played into the penalty area. Both Mora and Bellingham landed right around 100; Sullivan is all the way up at 202. Only Yamal, at 254, played more.

Scoring goals, creating chances, moving the ball into the attacking third, moving the ball into the box -- that's all there. The only thing missing is an ability to find space off of the ball, and it's only missing because I haven't mentioned it yet.

Sullivan has taken 142 touches inside the box. Among this cohort, Yamal, again, is the only player with more.

78 rating
The best players in modern soccer are the wide attackers who score goals, create chances, move the ball into attacking positions and find space inside the box. The best attacking prospects -- players in their late teens and early 20s -- tend to be able to score and create goals at a young age, but that's it. They usually can't aid in buildup play -- outside of slowing things down with a succession of head-down dribbles that sometimes move the ball upfield but often kill attacks by allowing the defense to recover. And they rarely have an advanced enough understanding of space and ball movement to be patient and savvy enough to receive passes in dangerous positions.

This all-conquering winger is a new prototype of player -- so new that the two best examples, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, are still playing. And so we haven't seen many young players develop with this idea in mind. That is, until Yamal -- and yes, now Sullivan.

The just-turned-17-year-old doesn't just have good-for-a-16-year-old numbers in his first real professional season. No, he genuinely has been one of the best players in MLS.

The player-rating model from the stats app Futi looks at how much every touch increases or decreases his team's chances of scoring and conceding a goal. Then it adjusts for the player's role and how well his team plays when he's on and off the field. And finally, they convert it all into an easy-to-understand 0-to-100 scale.

Among players with at least 1,500 minutes played this season, Sullivan currently ranks in the top 10 for the Futi model. The average age of the players ahead of him is nearly twice his: 31. And that's all for the full season; if we looked only at the post-World-Cup stretch, he probably would be even higher:

There are still plenty of questions.

Will he grow? What happens when he has moved beyond Philadelphia's relatively chaotic system? How might he handle moving and living in Europe? Those questions -- and more -- would hold true for any 16-year-old soccer player.

But while it probably won't happen because it's an unlikely outcome for everyone who has ever lived, Sullivan's early-career excellence means that he is more likely to become a superstar than any American who has come before him.

Just consider this. Futi also rates each individual area of a player's in-possession performance: shooting, creating, receiving, dribbling and linking (or buildup play). There are two players in the league who rate above a 60 in all five.

The two: Cavan Sullivan and Lionel Messi.

stories.headline: 'I love this game': Ben Simmons rejects NBA criticism
stories.summary: A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.
stories.body:
A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.

The Australian guard is back in the big league this year, having signed a $US3.5 million ($A4.9 million) deal with the Sacramento Kings.

Simmons purchased a controlling stake in a professional sport fishing team and didn't touch a basketball during his year off, in moves that drew plenty of criticism.

But the 30-year-old, who has been ravaged by injuries during his decade-long career, insists the break was purely about rebuilding his physical and mental health.

"It wasn't about if I wanted to play," Simmons told reporters at the Kings' preseason media session on Tuesday (AEST).

"All these people talk about how I don't love the game - that's bull----.

"I love this game. If I didn't, I wouldn't have taken that year to focus on myself and get back to where I'm at."

Simmons added he's not worried by critics chasing clicks from his name, declaring he's ready to prove to the world how much he missed basketball.

"I get to come out here and be creative and play hard and compete against a numerous amount of talented guys, so for me it's just in my blood and I've been doing it since I was a baby."

Simmons - a former No.1 overall draft pick, rookie of the year and three-time All-Star - believes the player he was at his peak "woke up" while he was out of the game.

And he's not short on confidence, bluntly outlining his personal goal this season.

"To dominate. Every time I step on the floor - to dominate," he said.

Simmons last played with the Los Angeles Clippers in April 2025 and took his year off as a result of persistent back and leg injuries, which took a significant toll on his body and mind.

The Melbourne-born star got serious in his comeback bid in August when he flew himself to a player-driven Boomers camp in his home town, where he impressed NBA scouts.

Sacramento pounced, signing Simmons on a one-season veteran league minimum deal.

"I'm right where I need to be," Simmons said.

"I took a lot of time to focus on my body over the season, and I think it's the best decision I've made for my career.

"I'm looking forward to getting going. I feel great, and I'm ready to go. No limitations."

Simmons expects to benefit from the low expectations on himself and the Kings, who were 22-60 last season and have only reached the playoffs once since 2006.

"It's really positive. There's no pressure," he said.

"They don't expect anything from us, so I think for us to go out there and show that we're capable of winning games and having a good team - that's doable.

"Based on this roster, I think we can do that."

Sacramento open the NBA preseason at home against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 5, and visit the Clippers for their regular-season opener on October 21.

Simmons' NBA comeback is also a step towards possible Australian Boomers selection for next year's FIBA World Cup in Qatar and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

stories.headline: Wests Tigers set to land David Bryenton after Bulldogs release

stories.body:
The Wests Tigers are set to land highly-rated teenager David Bryenton after he agreed to terms on a two-year deal from 2027, ESPN has learned.

Bryenton is finalising his release from the Canterbury Bulldogs, clearing the way for the young fullback to join Benji Marshall's side.

Marshall is understood to be a strong admirer of Bryenton and sees him as part of the Tigers' future.

The move resolves months of uncertainty for Bryenton, who left Canterbury's program earlier this year and returned to Queensland. He subsequently made two appearances for the Ipswich Jets in the Hostplus Cup.

Bryenton was among the country's standout schoolboy players in 2025. He represented the Australian Schoolboys and was named the Mal Meninga Cup player of the year before his anticipated move to the Bulldogs.

His agreement with the Tigers gives him a fresh start under Marshall and brings one of the game's most promising young fullbacks into the club's ranks for the next two seasons.

ESPN reported earlier this month that the club had also shown interest in off-contract Newcastle forward Tyson Frizell as it looks to strengthen its squad for next season.

stories.headline: What has gone wrong for the Patriots' offense, Drake Maye?
stories.summary: New England is last in the NFL in offensive points per game at 9.7. Can Maye and his supporting cast settle things down and turn it around?
stories.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had committed his third turnover, which was quickly turned into a touchdown, and was preparing to take the field again late in the third quarter of Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars.
Before he did, there was a moment on the sideline with head coach Mike Vrabel, who looked directly into Maye's helmet as he wrapped both of his arms around the quarterback's shoulder pads, play-sheet still in his left hand. Vrabel was doing his best to uplift Maye, whose start to the season has unexpectedly spiraled downward with six interceptions and a lost fumble. The defending AFC champions are now 1-2 heading into Sunday's road game against the 3-0 Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, CBS).

What has happened to Maye?

He had said his comfort level entering the second season in coordinator Josh McDaniels' offense was high, but he has looked mostly uncomfortable -- which has led to poor decision-making, defenses successfully pressing him and myriad miscues as he has navigated injuries to No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown and other core players around him. Maye called the offense "unacceptable" -- the unit ranks last in the NFL in points per game (9.7) -- and said he planned to "look in the mirror and take this as a turning point."

Vrabel cited a golf analogy in identifying one place for him to start.

"I think sometimes, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we're so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we're squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways," Vrabel said on sports radio WEEI.

"We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren't there."

Maye's struggles have contributed to the Patriots scoring the third fewest points through three games by a reigning conference champion in the Super Bowl era; their 36 trail only the 1999 Falcons (28) and 2007 Bears (33) Their 0.97 points per drive makes them the first team with less than one point per drive through three games since the 2021 Jets quarterbacked by Zach Wilson. And their minus-0.21 EPA per play is the worst by any team through three games since the 2023 Jets.

Teammates and coaches have consistently mentioned that the team's early-season challenges aren't solely on Maye, though.

"I think this is just an offensive unit deal, a team thing," receiver Romeo Doubs said. "The fundamentals are key ... fundamentals aren't strong enough. I keep emphasizing on it because that's part of this league, this game. You cannot win games doing your own thing. You have to have some sort technique and some professional initiative to get things rolling."

Maye has no touchdowns and five interceptions when targeting wide receivers, a group adjusting to being without Brown since early in the third quarter of the season opener at Seattle due to a right high ankle sprain. In the past two games, Maye has targeted Mack Hollins a WR-high 11 times, followed by Doubs (8), DeMario Douglas (7), Kyle Williams (5) and Efton Chism III (3). Hollins has led the group with eight receptions (for 108 yards) while Doubs has the most receiving yards with 145 (on six catches). According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Patriots receivers rank 30th in average route speed at 12.85 mph when passes are completed to them.

Brown, who was present in the locker room Monday and walking with a normal gait according to observers, is out for at least the next two games while on injured reserve. Sources familiar with his injury wouldn't be surprised if his absence extends beyond that, but players' recoveries often vary, and Brown was wearing cleats and a small ankle wrap Monday.

The running game, meanwhile, has flashed at times but has been too inconsistent (tied for 19th in the NFL at 3.9 yards per carry). And blocking has also been an issue. Maye was pressured on 47% of his dropbacks against the Jaguars, according to ESPN Research, which is his highest total this season and the fourth highest of his career. Overall, Maye has been pressured on 41.4% of his dropbacks, up from 33.9% in 2025. His off-target percentage against pressure is a whopping 36%, up from 17% last season. That ranks 26th in the NFL.

Losing starting right guard Mike Onwenu to a broken right ankle in the first half of a Week 2 win over the Steelers created a sizable void at the line of scrimmage. And then his replacement, veteran Greg Van Roten, was knocked out of Sunday's loss with a thigh injury in the second quarter.

Another factor in Maye's early-season struggles? How defenses are scheming against him.

ESPN Research noted that Maye faced zone on 51% of his dropbacks last season, but that has jumped to 65% this season. Specifically, defenses' usage of Cover 2 with two deep safeties to take away the long ball has increased from 19% last season to 32% this year. Maye dominated against man coverage in 2025, leading the league with an 89.2 QBR, 68% completion percentage and 9.0 yards per attempt. His 23 passing touchdowns against man looks ranked second in the NFL behind MVP Matthew Stafford (34). But now Maye is seeing way more zone coverage.

"We have to get this thing right, by all of us," Vrabel reiterated, adding he has had no thoughts of giving Maye a break on the sidelines.

Teammates continue to rally behind Maye, too: "That's my quarterback. When I got here, I was excited to work with him. And I look forward to growing with him," Doubs said.

So, what now? Vrabel pointed to the practice field when asked how he might help Maye loosen his grip on the golf club.

"Confidence comes from your preparation, and it comes from going out there. I can't manufacture confidence," he said. "You have to practice. You have to hit those plays in practice and you have to feel good about it.

"We just have to be able to make sure that we're on the same page, that everybody knows what is expected of them, have a few details, and then go play football."

The challenge ahead for Maye is amplified by the teams the Patriots face -- a trip to the undefeated Bills in the third-ever game in Buffalo's new stadium, then a home game against the resurgent 3-0 Raiders. Drop one of those games, and the Pats will have already matched their loss total from all of 2025. Lose both, and it would put them in a most vulnerable spot to defend their AFC championship.

stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 2

Practice One: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

stories.headline: Mets exec David Stearns: No 'mulligans' on Pete Alonso exit
stories.summary: David Stearns doesn't get a do-over. He knows that all too well, especially when it comes to getting players back that his organization let get away.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- David Stearns doesn't get a do-over. He knows that all too well.

One day after the New York Mets finished last in the National League East for the first time in 23 years, the team's embattled president of baseball operations was asked a pointed question.

Knowing what he knows now, would he have taken a full swing at re-signing Pete Alonso?

"I think that's a very fair question. The truth is in this job, I don't get mulligans," Stearns said Monday. "I also recognize Pete had a tremendous year. And the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough."

When the Mets didn't attempt to retain Alonso in free agency last fall, their homegrown franchise home run leader bolted for a five-year, $155 million contract with Baltimore as Stearns focused on improving the pitching and defense instead.

"I think I'll retire the phrase 'run prevention,'" Stearns said with a grin. "I don't know that that one worked particularly well."

Alonso topped the American League with 43 homers and 113 RBIs, playing in every game for the third consecutive season as the 31-year-old slugger became the first player in major league history to win an RBI crown in both leagues.

New York, meanwhile, never recovered from a 12-game losing streak in April. Despite a record $358 million payroll when the season began, the Mets struggled badly at the plate, were mediocre on the mound and finished 74-88 for their worst mark since 2017.

"This past weekend that we just experienced in Washington, where you are literally playing out the string, it's miserable. That is a miserable experience for players, for coaches, for executives," Stearns said during a 33-minute news conference at Citi Field to wrap up the season.

"I think we have an extraordinarily motivated organization, from ownership on down, to ensure that never happens again."

The absence of Alonso at first base was magnified when lineup mainstays Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor were sidelined for long stretches because of calf injuries.

Soto finished with a .908 OPS, the second lowest of his career, while Lindor set full-season career lows with 49 RBIs, three stolen bases, a .225 batting average and a .733 OPS.

Mets first basemen had 18 homers, 77 RBIs and a .667 OPS -- the third-lowest OPS at the position, ahead of only Seattle and Arizona.

Alonso received standing ovations from Mets fans before every at-bat during the Orioles' three-game sweep at Citi Field this month. He took a rare curtain call on the road Sept. 15, when his 300th career homer tied the score for Baltimore in the ninth inning and chants of "Fire Stearns!" rang out from the crowd of 28,097.

Last week, the Mets added former Minnesota Twins president of baseball operations Derek Falvey to the front office when he was hired as senior adviser for baseball operations. Falvey will report directly to Stearns.

New York played better late in the season, going 27-22 after the Aug. 3 trade deadline despite a massive selloff and 40-41 overall record under Andy Green, who took over as interim manager when Carlos Mendoza was fired June 26.

Green was given the full-time gig and a three-year contract last week.

Part of the improvement was fueled by rookie outfielders Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing, who combined for 31 homers and 47 stolen bases while playing strong defense. Rookie pitcher Nolan McLean went 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA in 31 starts.

But going into a critical offseason for Stearns, the Mets have major questions at first base, second base, in the bullpen and the rotation.

"Over the second half of the season, last few months of the season, we saw some really encouraging signs and we saw some elements of our team take shape that gives us all great optimism for both the near- and long-term future," Stearns said.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: No Cavan? No problem for surging Philadelphia
stories.summary: Philadelphia lost three star youngsters to international duty, yet the Union continued their march toward the top of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Hany Mukhtar became the 16th player in MLS history to score 100 goals after netting twice in a 2-0 win against Toronto. With seven games to go, Nashville is ten points clear (although Vancouver has a game in hand) as the Music City side seek its first Supporters' Shield.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

STL had the weekend off while it prepares for the Red Bulls on Wednesday.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

Despite a 3-0 win against RSL last weekend, it's been a so-so string of results for the Whitecaps after drawing D.C. 3-3. That's one win in four games across all competitions, although it's still mathematically possible to steal the Shield from Nashville.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Miami (and Lionel Messi, with an incredible free-kick goal, of course) helped close out the weekend with one of the more entertaining games of the matchday. But Miami walked away with a 2-1 loss to Columbus after a 98th-minute winner from the Crew. Santiago Morales getting sent off for time wasting two minutes earlier didn't help.

5. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

In a battle of two teams that are soaring in the second half of their season, Philly came out the victor in a 4-2 win against Orlando. With three players on international duty with the United States (including Cavan Sullivan, the team's second-highest goal contributor), Milan Iloski and Indiana Vassilev balled out, both clocking three goal contributions each with the former netting a hat trick.

6. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 5

After losing 3-0 in Utah, New England's first loss in four games came against a struggling RSL side. With a chunk of the Revolution's starting XI on international duty, including two of their three top goal contributors, it's a stumble but not a nose dive.

7. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 8

Charlotte's 1-0 loss at home to fifth-place Chicago could prove pivotal as we get closer to the playoffs. With the defeat, the fourth-place Crown is just one point ahead of the Fire in the Eastern Conference, and in picking up a late red card, Tim Ream will be absent for Charlotte's next game.

8. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 9

With Houston already trailing, Héctor Herrera's needless red card just before halftime did little to inspire a second-half comeback in a 2-0 defeat to SKC.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 7

With six players on international duty, including both top scorers, LAFC fell 1-0 to Dallas. With one win in ten games, Black and Gold announced they've parted ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 10

Antoine Griezmann was back in the starting lineup against Philadelphia after missing one match and contributed an assist, but it wasn't enough to get back in the win column. After the 4-2 defeat, Orlando has lost two straight games by that same scoreline. It's a shift from its five-game undefeated run, which ended with its U.S. Open Cup loss to Columbus, but it has a chance to make amends, starting with Columbus next weekend.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 11

Chicago's 1-0 win against Charlotte is its first in eight games across all competitions, but it puts the Fire within reach of a top-four spot in the East, as they now trail fourth-place Charlotte by one point. Johan Gómez scored the difference-maker off a corner to mark his first goal tally since returning from the Bundesliga.

12. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

Without key players (including the league's second-highest scorer, Petar Musa) Dallas beat LAFC 1-0 with a roaring header from Osaze Urhoghide off a corner. Ironically, the Black and Gold's late would-be equalizer that was called off for a light foul came from a corner, too.

13. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 12

Dropping points in a 2-2 draw against almost-bottom-of-the-East Atlanta will grate as the Pigeons hover just above the playoff line. As ATL's late equalizer came off a goalkeeping mishap, the absence of Matt Freese (on international duty for the U.S.) was keenly felt.

14. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 17

With a brace from Preston Judd (his fourth goal in three games), San Jose stretched its undefeated streak to six games after a 3-1 win against Portland. Every point counts as the playoffs loom; the Quakes finished the weekend in the West's top four, but two teams trail by just one point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 15

After notching a 3-2 come-from-behind victory against Colorado, the Galaxy have two straight 3-2 wins against teams vying for playoff positions. Those points could matter down the line, as they finish the weekend even with the Rapids, who still sit just above them in the table.

16. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 13

With six players missing for international duty, Cincinnati's defensive troubles continued in a 3-1 defeat to the Eastern Conference's last-placed team, Montréal. Cincy has now conceded 17 goals in its past five games. Success in the final third can only do much when you're that leaky at the back.

17. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

San Diego was sailing toward a 3-0 win until the 73rd minute, when it let Austin launch a late comeback in a 3-3 stalemate. SDFC now have two draws in two games but haven't won since Aug. 29. They could have used the three points: they've got seven games to break into the playoff positions but are three points and three places short of the wild-card spots in a very competitive Western Conference.

18. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 20

After beating Minnesota 3-1, Seattle has two wins in two games (including a midweek victory over RSL) and is undefeated in seven. And if it wasn't for Drake Callender's five saves, they would have scored more. With a game in hand, it finished the weekend just inside wild-card positions out west.

19. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

RSL got their first regular-season win since May 16 in a 3-0 victory over the Revs. As the team looks for answers, 19-year-old Aiden Hezarkhani opened the scoring early to mark his first tallies since March, while Sergi Solans notched a brace to mark his first since mid-August.

20. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 21

Brandon Vázquez scored a late diving header that inspired a three-goal comeback (Christian Ramírez had the others) in a 3-3 draw against San Diego. Not a bad way for Vázquez to score his first of the season.

21. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

RBNY took the weekend off but play again on Wednesday.

22. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 23

After closing out the weekend with a last-minute goal to seal a 2-1 win over Miami, Columbus is on a bit of a roll. The Crew have three wins in three games across all competitions, putting them four points (but still three places) shy of the wild-card spots in the Eastern Conference playoff race.

23. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 22

Paxten Aaronson isn't on Mauricio Pochettino's experimental young USMNT roster this month, but he registered his third goal and fifth goal contribution in four games in a 3-2 loss to the Galaxy. That's a small high note in a loss that could matter in the coming weeks, as the seventh-place Rapids are now even on points with eighth-place LA with seven games to go.

24. Minnesota United
